newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-FACTS FOR REAL MADRID-BARCELONA GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-FACTS FOR REAL MADRID-BARCELONA GAME.

text.p: Facts and figures for the Real Madrid-Barcelona Spanish first division match to be played on Saturday.
Real Madrid: Founded in 1902.
Major honours: League champions (record 26 times): 1932,
1987, 1988, 1989, 1990, 1995. Spanish Cup winners (17 times):
1985, 1986. Intercontinental Cup 1960.
Ground: Santiago Bernabeu stadium (named after club president
in glory days of 1950s and 60s), capacity 106,000.
Manager: Fabio Capello (Italy).
Record appearances: Carlos Santillana, 461.
Record goalscorer: Alfredo di Stefano, 218.
Barcelona: Founded in 1899 by a Swiss resident in
Barcelona, Hans Gamper.
Major honours: League champions (14 times): 1929, 1945,
1993, 1994. Spanish Cup winners (22 times) : 1910, 1912, 1913,
Champions: 1992. Cup Winners' Cup: 1979, 1982, 1989. Fairs Cup
(now UEFA Cup): 1958, 1960. 1966. European Supercup: 1993.
Ground: Camp Nou stadium, (meaning the 'new ground' in the
Catalan language), capacity 112,000.
Manager: Bobby Robson (England)
Record league appearances: Migueli, 391
Record goalscorer: Cesar Rodriguez, 174
Meetings between the sides:
Real Madrid have won 44 of their 66 home league games
against Barcelona, with 11 draws and 11 Barcelona wins. (There
have been 11 draws, 16 Real wins and 39 Barcelona victories in
games played in Barcelona).
Last year's game: Real Madrid 1 (Raul Gonzalez 13th minute)
Barcelona 1 (Roger Garcia 32nd). Attendance 106,000.
Last 10 seasons (starting in 1986, Real Madrid first): 1-1,
Fascinating facts:
--Barcelona were the first-ever Spanish league champions in 1929 and share with Real Madrid and Athletic Bilbao the honour of never having been relegated from the Spanish first division.

--Barcelona boast the largest number of season-ticket holders of any club in Europe -- 108,000 -- and averaged gates of 81,000 last season. Real have 70,000 season-ticket holders and averaged gates of 69,000.

--Barcelona's Camp Nou held the final of the 1992 Olympic tournament -- in which Spain beat Poland -- and the opening ceremony of the 1982 World Cup. The World Cup final, between Italy and West Germany, was played in the Santiago Bernabeu, which had also been the scene of Spain's 1964 European Nations Cup triumph over Russia.
--The reserve teams of both Barcelona and Real play in the Spanish second division, but would only be promoted if the first teams were relegated.

With the wealth of foreign stars now arriving in the first side, many younger players move on from the Real and Barcelona reserve sides to other teams. Over 40 such players are currently active in the Spanish first and second divisions.

--Barcelona reserves play in the Mini estadi, a 16,500-seat stadium adjoining the Camp Nou that is considerably bigger than several first division grounds. Real's reserves play in the 'Ciudad Deportiva' (sports city), a centrally located complex, part of which is to be sold off to pay Real's debts, which are estimated at 12 billion pesetas ($91.4 million).
--Barcelona games always begin with the singing of the club hymn, which is written in the local Catalan language..

Jordi, the patron saint of Catalonia, is a favourite name for local boys. Then Barcelona player, and later coach, Johan Cruyff followed tradition by naming his newly-born son -- now a striker at Manchester United -- after the saint.

--The Barcelona organisation also includes teams involved in several other sports. Barcelona's basketball and handball teams are among the most successful in Europe, and there are also roller-hockey, hockey, ice-hockey, athletics, rugby, baseball, indoor football, volleyball and skating sides.
--Real Madrid's basketball side has been just as successful in the European Cup as the football outfit, but the club no longer has other sports teams associated with it.

--Although few people would dispute that Argentine striker Alfredo di Stefano was Real's greatest-ever player, he may not be the most famous. Latin singing idol Julio Iglesias was once a goalkeeper for one of the club's reserve teams, and only took up music because of an injury.
